title: From Finite-Node Conifold Geometry to BPS Structures IV: Finite Charge Sectors and Primitive Node Data
content: We show that the finite-node conifold package extracted in earlier work canonically determines, through its inherited primitive node basis, a finite rational charge sector. More precisely, the nodewise primitive basis \( \{e_p\}_{p\in\Sigma} \) induces a rational charge space \( \Gamma_{\Sigma,\mathbf Q}\cong \bigoplus_{p\in\Sigma}\mathbf Q\gamma_p \) compatible with the localized schober sectors \( C_p \), the primitive lines \( K_0^{\mathrm{prim}}(C_p) \), the motivic primitive shadows \( Q_p \), the mixed-Hodge primitive blocks \( Q_p^H \), and the inherited state, support, and graded interaction packages \( (A_\Sigma,I_\Sigma^{(0/1)},I_\Sigma^{\mathrm{gr}}) \). We then analyze natural candidate pairings and formulate an integral refinement criterion: the rational charge sector descends to a preferred lattice only when the selected inherited structures are integral in the distinguished primitive basis. Low-node examples illustrate the resulting charge-sector package, its positive cone, candidate pairings, and the point at which integrality becomes additional structure. The finite rational charge sector constructed here is the algebraic input for subsequent work on stability data, chamber-wall structure, finite-node BPS sectors, and wall crossing.
